How to sew a zipper: pouch, bag, pillow, skirt and dress

Six ways to sew a zipper in, step by step: the lined zipper pouch, end tabs and the recessed zipper for pouches and bags; the centered, the lapped and the invisible zipper for a seam in a pillow cover, a skirt or a dress. Each way is animated, with advice on when to choose it. Use a zipper foot for the tabs, recessed, centered and lapped zippers, and an invisible zipper foot for the invisible one.

Lined zipper pouch

The outer, the zipper and the lining are sewn with one seam — then the other side of the zipper the same way.

When to choose it

When you make a makeup bag, a pencil case or a small bag with a lining: the zipper goes in together with the lining, and its tape and the seam allowances end up hidden inside.

Overview

Lined zipper pouch

The makeup bag's zipper, sewn in: the outer on one side, the lining on the other, a seam on each side of the zipper — and the zipper open, ready for the side seams. Tap to close the zipper.

  1. 1Outer — cotton · its 23 cm (9 in) side goes to the zipper
  2. 2Zipper — 20 cm (7⅞ in) · in the middle of the 23 cm side, its ends short of the side edges
  3. 3Lining — the same size as the outer
  4. 4Seams — 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in), one on each side of the zipper · no topstitching

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Lay the outer right side up.

    Put the zipper face down along one 23 cm (9 in) side, its edge on the edge of the fabric.

    Centre it: the 20 cm (7⅞ in) zipper is shorter than the side, so its ends stop short of the side edges and stay out of the side seams.

  2. Lay the lining face down on top of the zipper.

    Its edge is level with the edge of the outer: outer, zipper, lining — three layers.

    Clip the layers together.

  3. Sew through the outer, the zipper and the lining, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

    No topstitching along the zipper.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Open the lining out, away from the zipper: the outer on one side, the lining on the other.

    Fold the outer in half, right sides together, and the lining in half the same way.

    Their other short sides now meet the other side of the zipper: outer, zipper face down, lining — as before.

  5. Clip the layers together and sew through them all, 0.5 cm (³⁄₁₆ in) from the edge.

    The outer and the lining are now one loop, joined by the zipper on both sides.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Slide the pull to the other end: the zipper is open.

    Leave it open: the side seams come next, and the bag is turned right side out through the zipper.

    The side seams and turning out are on the makeup bag's page — the link is under this figure.

In the projects

Where it's used

  • A makeup bag with round corners: steps 7–8

Many instructions also topstitch along the zipper, so the fabric does not catch in the teeth; this makeup bag has no topstitching.

Zipper with end tabs

Small fabric tabs close both ends of the zipper before it is sewn in.

When to choose it

When you want neat, flat ends on a makeup bag or a pencil case: the tabs cover the zipper ends, so they stay out of the side seams and the corners lie flat.

Overview

Zipper with end tabs

Both ends of the zipper are closed with small fabric tabs, stitched just past the stops. Tap to lift the tabs.

  1. 1Tab — a strip of fabric folded like bias tape · a little wider than the zipper tape
  2. 2Stitching — along the folded edges of the tab, past the stop
  3. 3Stop — never sewn over
  4. 4Zipper — its ends inside the tabs

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut a short strip of fabric a little wider than the zipper tape: the tab covers the end of the zipper from edge to edge.

    You need two: one for each end of the zipper.

    Patterns give different sizes for the tab; what matters is that it is a little wider than the zipper tape.

  2. Lay the strip wrong side up.

    Fold two opposite edges in so they meet in the middle, wrong sides together.

    Press the folds with the iron.

  3. Fold the strip in half along the middle, so the folded edges meet inside.

    Press: the tab now has a fold on one side and the two folded edges on the other.

    Make the second tab the same way.

  4. Open the tab a little and slip the end of the zipper inside, right up to the fold.

    The folded edges come just past the stop, not over it.

    The tab sticks out a little on both sides of the zipper.

  5. Put on the zipper foot: it lets you stitch close to the folded edges.

    Stitch across the tab, close to its folded edges, through all its layers and the zipper tape.

    Keep the stitching on the tape, past the stop: never sew over the stop or the teeth. They are often metal, and the needle can break.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Slip the second tab over the other end of the zipper, the folded edges just past the stop.

    With the zipper foot, stitch along the folded edges, not over the stop.

    The rest is sewn as in the first way, the lined zipper pouch: the link is under this figure.

    Machine: straight stitch

Then the zipper is sewn in like the lined zipper pouch: the outer, the zipper and the lining with one seam, then the other side the same way. The side seams go just next to the tabs. 1Lined zipper pouch ↑

Recessed zipper at the top of a bag

The zipper is sewn between strips of fabric into a panel, and the panel goes inside the top of the bag, below the edge.

When to choose it

When you sew a tote or a big bag with a lining and want it to open wide, with the zipper below the edge. It goes into almost any lined bag; on very thick fabric the closed ends can be bulky.

Overview

Recessed zipper at the top of a bag

The zipper sits in a panel below the top edge of the bag, and the panel is sewn to the lining. Tap to open the zipper: the bag opens wide.

  1. 1Panel — four strips as long as the top edge of the bag · the zipper in the middle
  2. 2Zipper — a little longer than the strips · its ends closed with tabs
  3. 3Lining — the panel is sewn to it
  4. 4Outer — joined to the lining as usual

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Cut four strips of fabric as long as the top edge of the bag: two for each side of the zipper.

    Patterns give different widths for the strips: the wider they are, the lower the zipper sits in the bag.

    Many patterns iron interfacing onto the strips, so the panel keeps its shape.

    Cut the zipper a little longer than the strips; a zipper by the yard can be cut to any length.

  2. Lay one strip right side up.

    Lay the zipper face down on it, the edge of its tape on the long edge of the strip.

    Lay the second strip face down on top, edges level: the zipper tape is now between two strips, right sides inward. Hold the layers with clips.

  3. Put on the zipper foot: it lets you sew close to the teeth.

    Sew along the long edge, through both strips and the zipper tape.

    Keep the seam on the tape, beside the teeth, not over them.

    Machine: straight stitch

  4. Fold the strips back from the zipper: the zipper now lies face up beside them.

    The two strips lie wrong sides together, the seam hidden between them.

    Press the strips away from the teeth, so the fabric stays out of the zipper.

  5. With the zipper foot, topstitch along the edge of the strip by the zipper, close to the teeth.

    The topstitching holds both strips flat and keeps the fabric away from the teeth.

    Machine: straight stitch

  6. Lay the two other strips right sides inward around the other zipper tape and sew along the edge with the zipper foot.

    Turn them out, press them away from the teeth and topstitch close to the teeth.

    The panel is ready: the zipper in the middle, two strips on each side.

    Machine: straight stitch

  7. Make two fabric tabs and slip them over the ends of the zipper, as in the second way, Zipper with end tabs.

    With the zipper foot, stitch each tab just past the stop, not over it: the stops are often metal, and the needle can break.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Mark the middle of the panel's long edges and of the top edges of the lining pieces.

    Lay one long edge of the panel on the top edge of a lining piece, right sides together, middle on middle, and hold them with clips.

    Sew along the edge. Sew the other long edge to the other lining piece the same way.

    The panel goes on the lining, not on the outer: so it ends up inside the bag, below the edge.

    Machine: straight stitch

  9. Join the outer and the lining at the top edge as usual for a lined bag; the panel goes in with the lining.

    The zipper sits below the top edge of the bag.

    Opened, the panel drops against the sides, and the bag opens wide.

The ends of the zipper are closed with fabric tabs, as in the zipper with end tabs: a strip folded like bias tape over each end, stitched just past the stop. 2Zipper with end tabs ↑

Centered zipper

The two folded edges of the seam meet over the zipper teeth, with a line of stitching on each side.

When to choose it

When you want the simplest way to put a zipper into a seam: a pillow cover or a pillowcase, a skirt, the center back seam of a dress. The zipper shows just a little on both sides.

Overview

Centered zipper

The two folded edges of the seam meet over the zipper teeth; a line of stitching runs along each side and across the bottom. Tap to see through the fabric.

  1. 1Fabric — two pieces joined by one seam · their folded edges meet over the teeth
  2. 2Stitching — along both sides and across the bottom, below the stop · the same distance from the seam line
  3. 3Seam — below the zipper, backstitched at the mark
  4. 4Zipper — face down under the seam, its teeth on the seam line

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Finish the raw edges of the seam first, so they do not fray.

    Place the two pieces right sides together, the edges even, and clip them.

    Lay the zipper along the seam line and mark the seam line at its bottom stop: the opening for the zipper ends at the mark.

  2. Sew the seam with a regular stitch, on the seam line, up to the mark.

    Backstitch at the mark: the seam must not come undone where the zipper ends.

    Machine: straight stitch

  3. Set the machine to its longest stitch: this is basting, it will be unpicked later.

    Sew the opening closed on the same seam line, from the mark to the top edge.

    The basting holds the opening closed while the zipper is sewn in.

    Machine: longest stitch

  4. Open the pieces out and turn them wrong side up.

    Press the seam allowances open, one to each side, along the whole seam, the basted part too.

  5. Lay the zipper face down on the pressed-open seam allowances.

    Put the teeth right on the seam line, the bottom stop at the mark.

    Pin the zipper tape to the seam allowances only, not to the pieces under them.

  6. Turn the work right side up: the zipper is underneath, its teeth under the seam line.

    Put on the zipper foot: it lets the needle stitch close to the zipper.

    Stitch along one side, the same distance from the seam line all the way, and across the bottom, below the stop: never over the stop.

    At the corner, stop with the needle down in the fabric, lift the foot, turn the work and go on.

    Machine: straight stitch

  7. A few stitches before the pull, stop with the needle down in the fabric.

    Lift the presser foot and slide the pull past the foot, behind the needle.

    Lower the foot and finish the side with the zipper foot.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Stitch along the other side, the same distance from the seam line, and the other half of the bottom, below the stop.

    Pivot at the corner with the needle down.

    Sew both sides in the same direction.

    Machine: straight stitch

  9. Unpick the basting stitches over the zipper.

    Press from the right side: the two folded edges meet over the teeth.

Lapped zipper

One side of the seam folds over the zipper and hides it, with one line of stitching beside it.

When to choose it

When you sew a zipper into the side seam of a skirt, a dress or trousers and want it out of sight: the overlap hides the zipper, which helps when its color does not match the fabric, and only one line of stitching shows.

Overview

Lapped zipper

One side of the seam, the overlap, covers the zipper: its folded edge lies on the seam line, and one line of stitching shows, along that side and across the bottom. Tap to see through the fabric.

  1. 1Fabric — two pieces joined by one seam · the overlap's folded edge on the seam line
  2. 2Stitching — one line: along the overlap side and across the bottom, below the stop
  3. 3Seam — below the zipper, backstitched at the mark
  4. 4Zipper — under the overlap, stitched twice to the underlap's allowance

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Finish the raw edges of the seam first, so they do not fray.

    Place the two pieces right sides together, the edges even, and clip them.

    Lay the zipper along the seam line and mark the seam line at its bottom stop: the opening for the zipper ends at the mark.

  2. Sew the seam with a regular stitch, on the seam line, up to the mark.

    Backstitch at the mark: the seam must not come undone where the zipper ends.

    Machine: straight stitch

  3. Set the machine to its longest stitch: this is basting, it will be unpicked later.

    Sew the opening closed on the same seam line, between the mark and the top edge.

    The basting keeps both sides of the opening on the seam line while the zipper is sewn in.

    Machine: longest stitch

  4. Open the pieces out and turn them wrong side up.

    Press the seam allowances open, one to each side, along the whole seam, the basted part too.

  5. Turn the work right side up.

    Choose the overlap: the side that will cover the zipper. The other side is the underlap.

    Fold the overlap back over the underlap, out of the way, so it is not caught in the next stitching.

  6. Fold the underlap's seam allowance out, so it lies flat past the seam line: only this allowance is under the zipper.

    Lay the zipper face down on the allowance, the teeth by the seam line, the bottom stop at the mark.

    Pin the zipper tape to the allowance.

  7. Put on the zipper foot: it lets the needle stitch close to the zipper.

    Stitch close to the teeth, through the zipper tape and the seam allowance only.

    Stitch the whole length of the zipper, but never over the bottom stop.

    Machine: straight stitch

  8. Turn the zipper face up: the seam allowance folds under the zipper.

    A small fold forms right beside the teeth, just past the seam line: the folded part is a little narrower than the seam allowance.

    Press the fold.

  9. Stitch close to the fold, through the seam allowance and the zipper tape only: the overlap stays folded back.

    Stitch the whole length of the zipper, but never over the bottom stop.

    Machine: straight stitch

  10. Bring the overlap back over the zipper: the basting keeps its folded edge on the seam line.

    The overlap covers the teeth and both lines of stitching on the underlap.

    Pin the overlap to the zipper tape under it, through all the layers.

  11. Stitch along the overlap side and across the bottom, below the stop, through all the layers: wide enough to clear the teeth and the pull.

    At the corner, stop with the needle down in the fabric, lift the foot, turn the work and go on.

    Do not stitch over the stop.

    Machine: straight stitch

  12. Unpick the basting stitches over the zipper.

    Press from the right side: the overlap covers the zipper, and only its own line of stitching shows.

Invisible zipper

From the outside only the seam line and the pull show: the zipper is sewn in with a special invisible zipper foot.

When to choose it

When you sew a dress, a skirt or a pillowcase and want the zipper out of sight, only its pull: it suits satin and dressy clothes. A regular zipper foot also works, but not as well. Not for thick fabrics or a seam under heavy strain.

Overview

Invisible zipper

From the outside the zipper does not show: only the seam line and the pull. Tap to see through the fabric.

  1. 1Fabric — two pieces joined at the seam line · no stitching shows
  2. 2Seam line — the coil hides in it · below the zipper, a plain seam
  3. 3Zipper — under the fabric · its tapes stitched to the seam allowances only
  4. 4Pull — the only part of the zipper that shows

Step-by-step instructions

  1. Do not sew the seam yet: the zipper goes into the open edges first.

    The seam below the zipper is sewn once the zipper is in.

  2. Take an invisible zipper a little longer than the opening.

    Open the zipper all the way.

    Turn it to the back and press the coil flat with a barely warm iron: a hot iron melts the coil.

  3. Lay one half of the open zipper face down on the right side of one piece.

    Put the coil right on the seam line, the tape on the seam allowance.

    Pin the tape in place.

  4. Put on the invisible zipper foot: the coil runs in one of the two grooves under it.

    Stitch from top to bottom, close to the coil, until the pull stops the foot.

    Backstitch there.

    Keep the coil in the groove: if the stitching catches the coil, the zipper will not close.

    Machine: straight stitch

  5. Lay the other piece right side up.

    Turn the first piece over onto it, right sides together, its seam allowance and the sewn half of the zipper folded back.

    Lay the free half of the zipper face down on the right side of the other piece, its coil right on the seam line.

    Match the top edges, and any cross seams: the zipper must not be twisted. Pin.

  6. Put the coil in the other groove of the invisible zipper foot.

    Stitch from top to bottom, close to the coil, until the pull stops the foot.

    Backstitch there. The coil stays out of the stitching.

    Machine: straight stitch

  7. Close the zipper all the way.

    It slides freely when the coil is not caught in the stitching.

  8. Put the pieces right sides together, the raw edges even.

    Change to the zipper foot.

    Start a little above and to the side of the end of the zipper stitching, and sew the rest of the seam.

    Machine: straight stitch

  9. Fold the seam allowances out.

    Stitch each end of the zipper tape to its own seam allowance only, not to the piece.

    Machine: straight stitch

  10. Open the pieces out and turn them right side up.

    From the outside only the seam line and the pull show.

What you'll need

Zippers (also by the yard), sewing clips, pins, an air-erasable pen, fabric scissors, an iron, the sewing machine and a set of presser feet with a zipper foot — the tools I personally recommend for these steps. For the invisible zipper you will also need an invisible zipper and an invisible zipper foot.
